**Tier G** — governance — identity, capability, delegation, audit · owned by `platform` · `public.docs_section_releases`

**One row is** One section of the /docs manual and who may read it. A row per registry section KEY; a section with no row is read as confidential by the database and the client alike, so a section added later is closed until a super admin opens it.

## Uniqueness

| Columns | Source | Constraint |
|---|---|---|
| `section_key` | column PRIMARY KEY | `docs_section_releases_pkey` |

## Constraints

These reject the row outright. A value that fails one of them does not arrive
partially or get corrected — the write fails.

| Constraint | Rule | Added by |
|---|---|---|
| `docs_section_releases_key_shape` | `CHECK (section_key ~ '^[a-z][a-z0-9-]*$')` | `20261001000002_docs_release_and_questions.sql` |
| `docs_section_releases_audience` | `CHECK (audience IN ('public','internal','confidential'))` | `20261001000002_docs_release_and_questions.sql` |

## Governance

| | |
|---|---|
| Read capability | any project member |
| Write capability | `super_admin` |
| Minimum project role | `viewer` |
| Tier transitions audited | **no** — invariant `audit-actor` is not met here yet |
| Row-level security | enabled |
| Policies on the table | 1 — **1 with no predicate** |

Read is open to anon and authenticated — the /docs gate needs it BEFORE sign-in to know whether a public section may render, and a row says only which sections are open, whose titles are already in the bundle. There is no write policy; the one writer is `admin_set_docs_section_audience`, which asserts an active super admin and writes an `admin_audit_logs` row naming them. `audited: false` means no data-plane trigger, which this tier-G table does not carry; the admin audit row is the record. What an audience protects is presentation, not secrecy: page bodies are compiled into the app bundle (PLAN.md §6.5).

> **What the database actually permits is wider than the row above.**
> 1 policy here grants access with
> **no predicate at all** (`USING (true)`), so the capability named above is what the
> product intends to check, not what the database enforces:
>
> - `docs_section_releases_read` — `SELECT` to `anon`, `authenticated`
>
> See PLAN.md D28: the application runs as the
> `anon` role with no auth session and the anon key ships in the frontend bundle, so
> closing these is a migration with an auth model behind it rather than a policy edit.
